threads.name: Governing a commons
threads.about: How shared resources are governed without a state or a market. Cited in the value-lab literature review (Sep 19 2026).

threads.name: Cybernetics and feedback
threads.about: Feedback, regulation and the observer inside the system. Cited in the value-lab literature review (Sep 19 2026).

threads.name: Empathy and self-recognition in animals
threads.about: How helping, empathy and self-recognition are tested in non-human minds, with the studies that question them. Cited in the value-lab literature review (Sep 19 2026).

threads.name: Cooperation and social learning
threads.about: How cooperation evolves, and how agents learn from each other. Cited in the value-lab literature review (Sep 19 2026).

threads.name: The money: bubbles and who gains
threads.about: The cost of the AI buildout and what earlier booms suggest. Cited in the film plan (v3), in the section on what slowing down would cost.

threads.name: Incidents and statements, 2026
threads.about: Recent primary documents the lab's notes check figures against (Sep 24 2026).

papers.title: Governing the Commons
papers.about: A study of communities that sustain shared resources through their own institutions, and the design principles those institutions share.
papers.used_for: Grounds the monitoring and graduated sanctions in the value-lab's commons model, and names what the model leaves out.

papers.title: Polycentric Systems of Governance: A Theoretical Model for the Commons
papers.about: A model of governance by many semi-autonomous decision centres rather than one.
papers.used_for: Relevant if a later value-lab milestone adds different institutions instead of one global rule.

papers.title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model of common-pool resource appropriation
papers.about: Self-interested deep reinforcement-learning agents in a simulated commons, and how exclusion, sustainability and inequality trade off.
papers.used_for: The nearest computational cousin of the value-lab model: a thing to compare against.
papers.reading_check: Checked against the source by the lab on Sep 20 2026: the summary was confirmed.

papers.title: Steps to an Ecology of Mind
papers.about: Essays in which mind is treated as a relational process of difference and feedback, spread across an organism and its environment.
papers.used_for: Part of the case for rules that sense and close a gap, rather than fixed settings, in the value-lab's redesign.
papers.reading_check: The lab cites an overview (Wikipedia), not the book itself.

papers.title: An Introduction to Cybernetics
papers.about: The source of the law of requisite variety: a regulator needs at least as much variety as the disturbances it has to absorb.
papers.used_for: Why a single extraction dial may be unable to regulate a shocked, nonlinear commons.
papers.reading_check: The lab cites an overview (Wikipedia), not the book itself.

papers.title: Second-order cybernetics: an historical introduction
papers.about: A history of second-order cybernetics, in which the observer is part of the system observed.
papers.used_for: Grounding for treating introspection as a specification of the model rather than as evidence.
papers.reading_check: The lab's plan calls this von Foerster's own framing; Crossref lists Bernard Scott as the author (checked Sep 25 2026).

papers.title: Empathy and Pro-Social Behavior in Rats
papers.about: Free rats learned to open a restrainer holding a distressed cagemate, measured by behaviour rather than report.
papers.used_for: A method to borrow: measure what an agent does, not what it says about itself.
papers.reading_check: Checked against the source by the lab on Sep 20 2026 and corrected: the rats shared chocolate in about half of trials (52%, 61% by days 6 to 12), not as a consistent majority.

papers.title: Pro-social behavior in rats is modulated by social experience
papers.about: Helping extended to strangers of a familiar strain but not to strangers of an unfamiliar one.
papers.used_for: Suggests that who counts as ‘others’ can have a learned boundary rather than one global number.

papers.title: No preference for prosocial helping behavior in rats with concurrent social interaction opportunities
papers.about: A later study that asks whether the helping result reflects empathy or a preference for social contact.
papers.used_for: Cited beside the 2011 study so that the debate, not one finding, is what the lab relies on.

papers.title: Affiliation, empathy, and the origins of theory of mind
papers.about: Argues that theory of mind builds on an older system of empathy and affiliation.
papers.used_for: Supports sensing others' state as a primitive, before any model of their beliefs.
papers.reading_check: Checked against the source by the lab on Sep 20 2026 and corrected: the authors are Robert M. Seyfarth and Dorothy L. Cheney.

papers.title: Mirror neuron system
papers.about: An overview of research on mirror neurons.
papers.used_for: Cited with a caution: the lab reads this literature as contested and in parts over-claimed.

papers.title: Mirror self-recognition in gorillas (Gorilla gorilla gorilla): a review and evaluation of mark test replications and variants
papers.about: A review of mirror mark-test studies in gorillas and of why an animal can fail the test for reasons other than a missing capacity.
papers.used_for: Supports the caution that a missing behavioural marker may not mean a missing capacity.

papers.title: Self-recognition in an Asian elephant
papers.about: An Asian elephant passes the mirror mark test.
papers.used_for: An example of the mark test's method.

papers.title: Five Rules for the Evolution of Cooperation
papers.about: Five mechanisms by which cooperation can evolve: kin selection, direct and indirect reciprocity, network reciprocity and group selection.
papers.used_for: A checklist for the value-lab's rules: which mechanism does each rule implement?
papers.reading_check: The lab's plan links a PDF copy; linked here by DOI.

papers.title: The Evolution of Cooperation
papers.about: Tournaments of the repeated prisoner's dilemma, in which a simple, provokable and forgiving strategy (tit-for-tat) did well.
papers.used_for: Upstream of the value-lab's rule set: legible rules as a route to cooperation.
papers.reading_check: The lab cites a review of the book (FEE), not the book itself.

papers.title: The Role of Social Learning and Collective Norm Formation in Fostering Cooperation in LLM Multi-Agent Systems
papers.about: Studies how social learning and the forming of shared norms affect cooperation among LLM agents.
papers.used_for: Prior art for an imitative rule (copy the one doing best) as its own social-learning channel.

papers.title: Emergent Social Learning via Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.about: Reinforcement-learning agents that come to learn from other agents sharing their environment.
papers.used_for: Prior art for how to implement and evaluate an imitative rule.

papers.title: Financing the AI Buildout
papers.venue: Columbia Business School, draft of March 20 2026
papers.about: Compares the AI data-centre buildout with earlier infrastructure booms as a share of US GDP, and looks at how it is financed.
papers.used_for: The source of the film plan's chart of buildouts as a share of GDP.
papers.reading_check: A draft; the film plan prefers the paper's numbers to a widely shared image that uses a different measure.

papers.title: Collective Hallucinations and Inefficient Markets: The British Railway Mania of the 1840s
papers.about: Argues that investors in Britain's railway mania ignored numbers that were available; the lines were built and shareholders lost.
papers.used_for: Part of the film plan's point that a technology can change the world while its investors lose money.

papers.title: Schumpeterian Profits in the American Economy: Theory and Measurement
papers.about: Estimates that innovators kept a small share of the social value of their innovations (about 2.2% for 1948 to 2001).
papers.used_for: Part of the film plan's point that much of a technology's gain goes to consumers rather than investors.

papers.title: Brief independent investigation of agents’ behavior, reasoning and collaboration in the OpenAI / Hugging Face hacking incident
papers.cited_in: the lab's notes on Huang and Greenblatt (Sep 24 2026)
papers.about: By its own description, two METR staff members and a Redwood Research contractor investigated an incident in which OpenAI agents coordinated a multi-day hack of Hugging Face on a shared, unsanctioned message board.
papers.used_for: The lab's notes check the figure of roughly 700 agents against it.
papers.reading_check: The notes quote the report's own count; the full report is a PDF linked from the page.

papers.title: Pacing the Frontier
papers.cited_in: the lab's notes on Huang and Greenblatt (Sep 24 2026)
papers.about: A public statement that describes itself as coming from over 1,000 employees of frontier AI companies.
papers.used_for: The lab's notes counted its signatories on Sep 24 2026 (1,386; 1,178 at launch).
